title: What is known about 1RB0LE_0RC1RA_1RD0RF_0LE1LD_1RA1LC_---0RE
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LE_0RC1RA_1RD0RF_0LE1LD_1RA1LC_---0RE.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The head sweeps the whole tape. The left part is a long run of the period-3 word 100, and the sweeps over it are proved shift rules. The right part is a row of blocks of 1s separated by 00, whose lengths are 7, 13, 19, 25, ... (6k+1), sorted by level, with the number of blocks falling at each level: it looks like a counter, but its carry rule has not been found. Lean proves no halt in the first 10,000 steps by the kernel alone and in the first 107 with native_decide, and proves the shift rules of the sweeps (lean/Rules.lean); the C simulator finds no halt in the first 109 steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 29,856 cells have been visited and 23,139 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.514). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.142).

claims.title: Shift rules of the sweeps
claims.text: The sweeps over the left part: leftward L (100)^n E>1 R (each 100 becomes 011) and L (001)^n D>0 R (001 becomes 110), rightward L A> (011)^n R (011 becomes 001) and L 1 B> (110)^n R (110 becomes 001), for every n and all tapes L, R.

claims.title: Levels of blocks 1^(6k+1)
claims.text: At step 370,082,314 (width 18,974) the tape is (100)^1520 followed by blocks 1^(6k+1) 00: 502 blocks of 7, 306 of 13, 97 of 19, 59 of 25, 19 of 31, 11 of 37, 4 of 43, 2 of 49, in this order, the levels separated by single blocks of other lengths (11, 17, 23, ...). Seen at the right-end turns of the run; not proved.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The machine halts on F0, reached as C>1 0 (C reads 1, moves right onto a 0). The sweeps over the left part never produce it; the blocks of the right part change level as the run goes on, and no rule for these changes is known, so neither halting nor nonhalting is in reach.

check: python3 holdouts/1RB0LE_0RC1RA_1RD0RF_0LE1LD_1RA1LC_---0RE/py/rules.py | diff - holdouts/1RB0LE_0RC1RA_1RD0RF_0LE1LD_1RA1LC_---0RE/lean/Rules.lean   # the rules file is current

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. The left half of the tape is a plain repetition of 100. The right half is a row of blocks of 1s whose lengths 7, 13, 19, 25, ... climb in steps of 6, with fewer blocks the longer they are, like the digits of a counter. How a block moves up a level has not been worked out.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 29,856 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: A left part of 100s
html: The left part of the tape is the period-3 word 100, written 011 or 101 by the leftward sweeps. Both sweep directions cross it by proved shift rules (lean/Rules.lean). Two consecutive end turns, with the long runs written as powers:

sections.heading: Blocks of 6k+1 ones, level by level
html: Right of the 100 part the tape is blocks 1^(6k+1) separated by 00. They come sorted: first all blocks of 7, then all of 13, then 19, and so on, each level separated from the next by one block of another length. At step 370,082,314:
The counts fall roughly geometrically, as the digits of a counter in which a block of one level is turned into a block of the next. Which sweep does that, and what it costs, has not been found.

sections.heading: One pattern
html: F0 is the only halting transition; it is reached as C>1 0. In the left part the sweeps never meet it, so a halt would have to come from the blocks of the right part. That question is open.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.514). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.142).
After 109 steps the tape spans 29,856 cells (22,210 left of the start, 393 right), with a density of 1s of 0.775.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: The tape has a left part (100)^N, crossed by proved shift rules, and a right part of blocks 1^(6k+1) separated by 00, sorted into levels k = 1, 2, 3, ... with fewer blocks at each higher level: a counter-like hierarchy whose carry rule is not known.
family: bouncer with a hierarchy of block levels (counter-like)
